items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: I have a friend, Willie Salor, his wife was the daughter of Mr. Harriton.

ctx.x: I’d like to jump forward a little bit, and this is a bit of a tangent but in 1963 I think you were 23, that was the year that Medgar Evers was assassinated. And I’m wondering, can you put into words how that affected you?

Well yeah. 1963 was the year that I graduated and got my bachelor’s degree. But prior to that I would eat lunch with Medgar Evers for three years from ’60 to ’63. There was a place called Smacko’s in Jackson on Nth Street. And Smacko’s was the place right across the street from Medgar Evers’ office, which was in the, we called it the State Office Building. And at lunchtime there were no fast food places, but people that didn’t go home for lunch went to cafes and they had home cooked meals there. And as a college…

And that was, oh a very devastating part of my life, you know he was killed because my youngest sister was in a meeting that night that he had organized the youth to go and do a sit-in down in the city in Jackson. Because the reason for that is my youngest sister was a teenager and I was an adult. I was 23 years old. Had I sit-in they would have sent me to the State penitentiary and booked me as a real criminal or something like that. But as a youth, teenagers, my sister, they could arrest them but they couldn’t…
